distractors.reason: 'Deeply' goes with feelings and emotions (deeply concerned, deeply moved), not with temperature. 'Deeply cold' sounds unnatural.
'Highly' is used with degrees of probability or quality (highly unlikely, highly recommended). We don't say 'highly cold'.
'Strongly' usually goes with opinions or beliefs (strongly opposed, strongly believe). We don't say 'strongly cold' for weather.

example_sentence: The wind was ___ cold this morning, so we wore our coats.
l1_interference: Osoby mówiące po polsku często używają 'very cold' lub 'highly cold' jako odpowiednika 'bardzo zimny'. Poprawnie w tym kontekście jest 'bitterly cold', gdzie 'bitterly' wyraża silne, dotkliwe zimno.
explanation: In English, 'bitterly' is used with cold weather and wind to show that the cold is severe and unpleasant. Each degree adverb has its own set of adjectives it usually combines with.

related_collocations.example: It is highly unlikely that it will snow in May.
The parents were deeply concerned about their son's health.
Many residents are strongly opposed to the new road.

memory_tip: BITTERLY = severe cold or harsh weather, bitter feelings | DEEPLY = strong emotions (concerned, moved) | HIGHLY = high degree of probability or quality (unlikely, recommended) | STRONGLY = firm opinions or beliefs (opposed, agree)
